title: ANC vs. NYC: We Put the Best Noise-Canceling Earbuds to the Ultimate Test
gist: Wired's buying guide, tested against New York City noise (subways, streets, cafes), crowns Bose's QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen, $299) as best overall ANC while naming category-specific winners across Anker Soundcore, Apple, Samsung, Google, Sony, Beats, and JLab at price points from $30 to $328.

insights.claim: Bose's QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen), priced at $299 ($249 on sale), are rated the best overall noise-canceling earbuds by Wired's testing, with the reviewer stating no competitor has yet dethroned them on pure ANC performance despite the Sony WF-1000XM6 coming close.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Bose retains category leadership in premium ANC earbuds against Apple, Sony, and Samsung, relevant to competitive positioning in the wireless audio market.
insights.quote: In all my testing, I've yet to find a pair of noise-canceling earbuds that can knock these off the throne, though some models come close.

insights.claim: The Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds' main weaknesses are large size (poor for workouts), high price, and mediocre battery life of only 6 hours with ANC on, versus 8 hours for Apple AirPods Pro 3 and Sony WF-1000XM6.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Battery life and form factor remain Bose's key competitive weak points versus Apple and Sony, a factor for consumers prioritizing all-day or workout use.
insights.quote: The QuietComfort Ultra is also pricey and doesn't have very impressive battery life (just six hours). But for ANC alone, it is the gold standard.

insights.claim: The Soundcore by Anker Liberty 5 Pro, at $170 ($150 on sale), delivers noise-canceling and call quality that outperformed every other wireless earbud tested on noisy city streets, alongside better battery life (6.5 hours ANC, 28 with case) and a higher IP55 water/dust rating than the pricier Bose model.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Anker's Soundcore sub-brand is closing the gap with premium players on call quality and durability at roughly half the price, pressuring margins in the mid-tier ANC earbud segment.
insights.quote: The biggest differentiator is call quality—these are some of the best earbuds for calls, full stop. They outperformed every other wireless earbud I tested them against on noisy city streets.

insights.claim: Apple's AirPods Pro 3 ($249) are recommended specifically for iPhone/Apple ecosystem users due to seamless cross-device switching, Find My network integration, and built-in heart rate sensors that the reviewer found surprisingly accurate versus Garmin and Google wearables; Apple has also newly added ANC to its entry-level AirPods 5.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Apple is pushing health-sensor features (heart rate) into earbuds as a wearables-adjacent play and extending ANC downmarket to AirPods 5, both relevant to Apple's wearables revenue mix.
insights.quote: They also have heart rate sensors built into each earbud, meaning you can start and track a workout and get accurate, detailed stats without wearing a fitness tracker. I've tested them against wearables from Garmin and Google, and they are surprisingly accurate.
insights.locator: Best ANC Earbuds for iPhone section

insights.claim: The JLab Audio Go Pop ANC, at just $30, is highlighted as the best cheap ANC earbud, with the reviewer noting no competing ANC earbuds have been found under $50, and the JLab model offers stable Bluetooth, adjustable EQ, IP55 rating, and decent battery despite only so-so noise cancellation.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Sub-$50 ANC remains a market gap outside of JLab, indicating room for price competition at the true entry level of the ANC earbud category.
insights.quote: I have yet to find competing noise-canceling earbuds for under $50. These JLab earbuds come close...

insights.claim: The Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro ($250) are explicitly recommended only for users within the Samsung ecosystem, since their features (GPS tracking, device swapping) closely mirror AirPods but only function fully with Samsung Galaxy phones.
insights.speaker: Ryan Waniata, via Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Samsung continues to use ecosystem lock-in (feature parity with AirPods, but Samsung-only) as its earbuds strategy rather than competing on cross-platform value.
insights.quote: I wouldn't recommend the Galaxy Buds for anyone outside of Samsung's ecosystem, though.
insights.locator: Best ANC Earbuds for Samsung section

insights.claim: The Sony WF-1000XM6 ($328) is rated the best-sounding wireless earbud tested, using memory foam ear tips for excellent passive isolation combined with near-Bose-level ANC, but loses the overall crown to Bose because achieving a proper fit required swapping ear tips multiple times.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Fit consistency, not raw ANC or audio quality, is the deciding factor keeping Sony from unseating Bose at the top of the category — a usability nuance for competitive benchmarking.
insights.quote: Still, the crown goes to Bose for the best ANC, simply because the 1000XM6 can be tricky to fit perfectly—I had to swap out ear tips a few times before they felt comfortable.
insights.locator: Best ANC Earbuds for Sound Quality section

themes.theme: How ANC and transparency mode actually work

insights.claim: Active noise cancellation works by using exterior microphones to detect incoming sound waves and generating an inverse waveform that cancels them out through destructive interference, a decades-old physics principle (ANC has existed since the 1970s) that has simply been refined with better hardware and software over time.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: Useful baseline framework for evaluating ANC marketing claims: differentiation among vendors comes from execution/tuning, not from a fundamentally new underlying technology.
insights.quote: ANC uses microphones to hear incoming waves and generate the polar opposite waveform. When you add opposite waveforms together, they cancel each other out, and it's as if there is no sound wave at all, at least to our ears.
insights.locator: FAQ: What Is Noise Canceling and How Does It Work?

insights.claim: Transparency/ambient sound modes, which let outside sound through, perform poorly in windy outdoor conditions (e.g., biking), producing distorted artificial wind noise, making open-style earbuds a better alternative for outdoor activities like running or biking.
insights.speaker: Harry Rabinowitz
insights.so_what: A concrete product limitation (wind interference with transparency mode) that segments the ideal use case for sealed ANC earbuds versus open-ear designs.
insights.quote: I've tried using transparency mode while riding an ebike, and it mostly sounds like a blistering blast of artificial wind noise.
insights.locator: FAQ: What Is Transparency Mode or Ambient Sound Mode?
